question: Which symptom is a classic sign of stress urinary incontinence after childbirth?

options.A: Passing large amounts of urine only at night
options.B: A constant burning sensation when passing urine
options.C: Leaking urine when coughing or sneezing
options.D: Inability to empty the bladder completely

explanation: You're doing great! Stress incontinence happens when sudden pressure (like a cough or sneeze) beats a tired, weakened pelvic floor.

question: What is the main goal of diagnostic testing for hormone (endocrine) disorders?

options.A: To destroy overactive hormone-producing tissue
options.B: To permanently replace missing organ functions
options.C: To cure infectious agents causing gland failure
options.D: To measure hormone levels and check organ response

explanation: You've got this! Endocrine tests simply check how much hormone is in the body and see how target organs respond to signals. It is all about checking the balance.

question: Where in the body would you look for multi-unit smooth muscle?

options.A: In the walls of the urinary bladder
options.B: In the iris of the eye controlling the pupil
options.C: In the muscular walls of the stomach
options.D: In the middle layer of the small intestine

explanation: Multi-unit muscle gives us fine, precise control—just like adjusting your camera lens or how your iris changes the pupil size in bright light!

question: Which two main proteins make up the tiny filaments inside a muscle sarcomere?

options.A: Collagen and elastin
options.B: Actin and myosin
options.C: Troponin and calcium
options.D: Myoglobin and hemoglobin

explanation: Actin (the thin one) and myosin (the thick one) are the dynamic duo inside your muscles that slide together to create movement. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h2)

question: What type of energy does an ultrasound machine use to create images inside the body?

options.A: Sound waves
options.B: Magnetic fields
options.C: Radioactive tracers
options.D: X-ray radiation

explanation: Ultrasound uses safe, high-frequency sound waves that bounce off your tissues to form a picture, meaning there's no radiation involved at all!

question: Why is it important for nurses to recognize the signs of the active dying phase?

options.A: To shift care goals toward maximum comfort and prepare the family
options.B: To start aggressive diagnostic blood tests right away
options.C: To transfer the patient back to the intensive care unit
options.D: To administer emergency resuscitation drugs immediately

explanation: Recognizing these signs helps us stop invasive procedures and focus entirely on keeping the patient peaceful and supporting their loved ones.

question: Which friendly bacteria is most commonly found keeping a healthy reproductive-age vagina happy and protected?

options.A: Staphylococcus
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Streptococcus
options.D: Lactobacillus

explanation: Lactobacillus is our hero bug here! It's the dominant, protective bacterium that keeps the vaginal environment healthy and balanced. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: How does acute physical or emotional stress falsely affect a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: It destroys red blood cells and ruins the laboratory blood samples
options.B: It releases hormones like adrenaline and cortisol that raise blood sugar
options.C: It slows down digestion so the stomach cannot absorb the glucose drink
options.D: It forces the pancreas to release too much insulin, causing severe hypoglycemia

explanation: Stress hormones mobilize stored energy and push blood glucose levels up, which can mimic diabetes during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h6)

question: Where is the best place on the body to give an emergency intramuscular shot of epinephrine?

options.A: Dorsal gluteal muscle
options.B: Anterolateral thigh
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Subcutaneous abdominal fat

explanation: Spot on! The outer-front part of the thigh (anterolateral thigh) absorbs medications into the bloodstream much faster and more reliably than other sites.

question: Why do large family sizes still hold a lot of cultural importance in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policies mandate a minimum number of children per household.
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable in rural areas.
options.C: They are viewed as a symbol of wealth and ancestral continuity.
options.D: Traditional healers require large families for spiritual protection.

explanation: Exactly! In many traditional settings, having a large family is celebrated as a sign of prosperity, strength, and keeping the family lineage alive.

question: What color should a nurse expect the patient's stool to be for the first couple of days after a barium meal?

options.A: Bright red or bloody
options.B: Jet black and tarry
options.C: Chalky white or pale gray
options.D: Dark green and watery

explanation: You're doing fantastic! Since barium is a heavy white mineral, it turns the poo a distinct pale or chalky color as it leaves the body. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: In a life-threatening poisoning emergency, which route of administration is generally preferred for antidotes?

options.A: Intravenous
options.B: Transdermal
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Rectal suppository

explanation: The IV route puts the antidote straight into the bloodstream so it can start working almost immediately when every second counts.

question: Where do water-soluble (peptide) hormone receptors usually sit?

options.A: On the outer cell membrane
options.B: Attached directly to cellular DNA
options.C: Inside the cell nucleus
options.D: Floating freely in the cytoplasm

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't slip through the oily cell membrane, they have to catch their receptors right on the outer surface of the cell.

question: A patient walks into the clinic with lower tummy pain and unusual discharge. What serious upper-body complication should a nurse watch out for if this is left untreated?

options.A: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: Iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: If a lower infection is ignored, it can travel upwards into the reproductive organs and trigger pelvic inflammatory disease (PID).

question: Why might a baby in Gallows traction have trouble breathing deeply?

options.A: The ropes block fresh air from their face
options.B: The sticky tape gives off lung-irritating fumes
options.C: The heavy weights make the room air too thin
options.D: The elevated legs push up on the tummy and limit lung expansion

explanation: Lifting those legs straight up presses the tummy contents against the diaphragm, which can slightly crowd the lungs. Good catch for nursing assessments!

question: What makes a low-profile gastrostomy device different from a standard PEG tube?

options.A: It does not require an internal retention bolster or balloon
options.B: It delivers liquid nutrition directly into the large intestine
options.C: It sits flush against the skin without long dangling tubing
options.D: It is placed permanently and can never be removed or changed

explanation: Button-type low-profile devices are discreet and popular with active patients because they lack the long external tubing of standard PEG tubes. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main difference between a teaching method and a teaching technique in the classroom?

options.A: A technique is decided by the school board while a method is chosen by the student
options.B: A method is the overall instructional strategy while a technique is the specific classroom action
options.C: A method deals with student grades while a technique deals with lesson planning
options.D: A technique is used only in the classroom while a method is used strictly at the bedside

explanation: Think of the method as your broad game plan for the class, while the technique is the specific move or action you use to pull it off during the lesson! You've got this.

question: What is the typical duration of antibiotic therapy for osteomyelitis?

options.A: 3 to 5 days
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: 4 to 6 weeks or longer
options.D: Exactly one year

explanation: Because antibiotics penetrate bone tissue slowly, treatment requires a prolonged course, usually lasting several weeks to clear the infection fully. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h7)

question: In a study on medication adherence for high blood pressure, what is the most likely dependent variable?

options.A: Age of the nurse
options.B: Color of the clinic walls
options.C: Blood pressure control
options.D: Distance to the clinic

explanation: The dependent variable is your outcome. Here, we want to see if the blood pressure is successfully controlled at the end of the day!

question: What is the main reason a nurse asks a patient about a family history of blood disorders?

options.A: To predict the exact date the patient will recover
options.B: To find out if family members can pay for hospital bills
options.C: To identify inherited conditions passed down through genes
options.D: To determine which hospital room the patient prefers

explanation: Conditions like haemophilia and sickle cell disease are passed down from parents to children through genes. Family history is a great shortcut to knowing what to look out for!

question: How does carrying extra body weight affect weight-bearing joints like the knees?

options.A: By drying out the synovial fluid completely
options.B: By stopping blood flow to the bone marrow
options.C: By increasing chemical toxins in the blood
options.D: By placing continuous mechanical stress on weight-bearing joints

explanation: Well done! Extra weight means extra physical pressure on joints like your knees and hips with every single step you take.

question: How can a nurse manager use substantive (task-focused) conflict in a positive way?

options.A: Transfer all experienced nurses away
options.B: Encourage open dialogue and constructive problem-solving
options.C: Ignore all disagreements on the ward
options.D: Punish everyone who participates in a debate

explanation: Work-related debates actually spark brilliant ideas when leaders guide the team to discuss them respectfully. Well done!

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse should do right away for a patient with sudden chest pain?

options.A: Administering supplemental oxygen
options.B: Having the patient rest immediately
options.C: Encouraging heavy physical exercise
options.D: Checking vital signs and an ECG

explanation: You got it! Exercise makes the heart work harder and crave more oxygen, which is the last thing an ischemic heart needs. Rest is always first!

question: A community nurse meets resistance from male elders who think family planning promotes promiscuity. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the elders completely and hand out contraceptives secretly behind their backs
options.B: Engage the men in respectful dialogue, emphasizing child spacing, maternal health, and family financial stability
options.C: Argue with them aggressively to prove that their traditional beliefs are entirely wrong
options.D: Report the entire village community to the local police station immediately

explanation: Community health nursing requires patience and respect. Sitting down to talk with community leaders helps frame family planning around health, peace, and family well-being.

question: Which group of blood pressure medications must be strictly avoided during pregnancy because they can harm the baby's kidneys?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Calcium channel blockers
options.C: ACE inhibitors
options.D: Centrally acting alpha agonists

explanation: Remember: ACE inhibitors are known to mess with how a baby's kidneys develop, so doctors steer clear of them during pregnancy.

question: What clinical advantage does seeing a patient at home give a nurse?

options.A: A chance to test all household appliances for electrical safety
options.B: Instant access to advanced surgical laboratories inside the bedroom
options.C: Direct observation of real-life living habits, diet, and daily mobility
options.D: The ability to order X-rays without consulting a medical doctor

explanation: Visiting the home reveals practical challenges like poor pantry stock or tripping hazards that a hospital room hides. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: A patient calls reporting a fever of 38.5°C and severe pelvic pain three days after a medical abortion. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: An ongoing uterine infection
options.B: An allergic reaction to ibuprofen
options.C: A normal side effect of mifepristone
options.D: A normal reaction to lingering hormones

explanation: Spot on! A lingering fever and severe pain days after the procedure can signal a uterine infection that needs a doctor's attention and antibiotics.

question: How do automated hospital beds make a nurse's duty easier?

options.A: By eliminating the need to ever document vital signs manually
options.B: By completely replacing the need for bedside nursing assistants
options.C: By making regular patient safety rounds completely unnecessary
options.D: By reducing physical strain during patient repositioning and transfers

explanation: Patient beds with automated features do the heavy lifting when turning or moving patients, saving your back from unnecessary strain!

question: A patient is having trouble controlling their body temperature and fluid balance. Which brain structure is likely involved?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Broca's area
options.C: Cerebellum
options.D: Hypothalamus

explanation: The hypothalamus is like your body's internal thermostat and control center for thirst, hunger, and temperature.

question: What skill helps a leader look past surface drama and find the real root cause of a ward problem?

options.A: Speed reading
options.B: Blind obedience
options.C: Critical thinking
options.D: Public speaking

explanation: Critical thinking is your detective tool. It helps you dig beneath surface complaints to figure out what is actually causing the trouble on the ward.

question: What is the main goal of doing routine data validation at your clinic?

options.A: Replacing paper registers with permanent digital tablets instantly
options.B: Catching and correcting recording errors before report submission
options.C: Speeding up the physical delivery of drugs from international donors
options.D: Increasing the financial grants given directly to individual nurses

explanation: Spot on! Validation is just our safety net to catch small mistakes early so our reports go up the chain clean and correct.

question: Which of these substances should you NEVER use to soothe dry nostrils during oxygen therapy because of fire risks?

options.A: Petroleum jelly
options.B: Aqueous cream
options.C: Water-based gel
options.D: Saline nasal spray

explanation: Never use petroleum-based products around oxygen! They are flammable and can easily catch fire in an oxygen-rich environment—always stick to water-based options.

question: Which of these tells you that a patient is getting too tired during active exercises?

options.A: Falling into a deep, heavy sleep instantly
options.B: Shortness of breath or dizziness
options.C: Skin turning bright pink and warm
options.D: A sudden increase in smiling and laughing

explanation: Watch out for breathlessness or lightheadedness—these are classic signs that the patient has had enough for now.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Sharp pain located exclusively in the upper right shoulder
options.B: Bilateral lower abdominal and pelvic pain
options.C: Severe itching of the external perineal skin
options.D: Painless swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Since both tubes can be affected, inflammation usually shows up as lower belly or pelvic pain felt on both sides.

question: Why does high prolactin stop a woman from releasing an egg during ovulation?

options.A: It blocks progesterone receptors in the uterus
options.B: It suppresses gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.C: It destroys the developing ovarian follicles directly
options.D: It increases estrogen to dangerous levels

explanation: Extra prolactin gets in the way of brain signals, halting the hormone needed to trigger ovulation. It's a completely natural process, like how the body pauses cycles during breastfeeding!

question: Which Nigerian agency relies heavily on routine disease reports and tracking to manage outbreaks?

options.A: Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
options.D: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC)

explanation: The NCDC is our national frontline defense, coordinating outbreak responses using data sent up from local health facilities.

question: Which statement is the best example of supportive communication for a grieving family member?

options.A: 'At least your loved one is no longer suffering in pain.'
options.B: 'You have to stay strong for the rest of your young children.'
options.C: 'Don't worry, you will eventually find someone new to love.'
options.D: 'I am so sorry for your loss; I am here if you want to talk.'

explanation: You've got this! Acknowledging their pain directly and just being present is comforting, whereas cliché phrases can sound dismissive.

question: What is a common barrier to maternal healthcare access driven by traditional gender norms in Nigeria?

options.A: Universal laws prohibiting women from entering clinics
options.B: A complete absence of medical facilities nationwide
options.C: Delayed spousal approval for healthcare finances
options.D: Biological immunity to pregnancy-related complications

explanation: Well reasoned! When men hold sole financial control, women sometimes have to wait for permission or money to get emergency obstetric care, which can be dangerous.

question: A patient in her second trimester feels the baby move for the first time and feels much more connected. What is this milestone called?

options.A: Quickening
options.B: Nesting
options.C: Ambivalence
options.D: Couvade

explanation: Well done! Quickening is that magical moment when fetal movement makes the pregnancy feel truly real.

question: Why might a patient be given a carbohydrate drink up to two hours before surgery?

options.A: To replace the need for intravenous fluids during the operation
options.B: To reduce insulin resistance and postoperative discomfort
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing surgical site infections
options.D: To completely fill the stomach so the patient feels full

explanation: Correct! Giving carbs before surgery helps calm fasting stress, keeps insulin working well, and cuts down on post-surgery nausea.

question: How can we best describe public health surveillance?

options.A: A method for punishing clinics that lose patient files
options.B: A financial audit of private clinic expenditures
options.C: An ongoing system of collecting and analyzing health data
options.D: A one-time yearly census of hospital bed capacity

explanation: Think of surveillance as a continuous watch, not just a one-off check. We keep gathering and reviewing health data day in and day out to stay ahead of sickness!

question: A community nurse sees children with swollen bellies due to severe protein shortages. What type of agent is causing this?

options.A: Biological agent
options.B: Chemical agent
options.C: Nutritional agent
options.D: Physical agent

explanation: When a disease is caused by missing essential nutrients in the diet (like protein), we call it a nutritional agent. You're doing great!

question: Which brain chemical do minor tranquilizers like benzodiazepines boost to help you calm down?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: GABA

explanation: Benzodiazepines team up with GABA—your brain's natural calming chemical—to slow down nervous system activity. Excellent nursing knowledge to keep in mind!

question: What does the term 'oophoritis' mean?

options.A: Swelling of the fallopian tubes
options.B: Cyst formation on the cervix
options.C: Inflammation of the ovaries
options.D: Infection of the uterine lining

explanation: You've got this! Oophoritis simply means inflammation of one or both ovaries, usually caused by an infection. Great start!

question: When body cells are completely cut off from oxygen, what backup energy system do they switch to?

options.A: Oxidative phosphorylation
options.B: Anaerobic metabolism
options.C: Glycolytic synthesis
options.D: Aerobic metabolism

explanation: When oxygen runs out, cells go into survival mode and use anaerobic metabolism. It keeps things going briefly, but makes lactic acid and less energy.

question: While checking a patient with a leg infection, you notice their toes are cool, pale, and slow to refill with blood. What is your best first move?

options.A: Apply a heating pad directly to the toes
options.B: Document the findings as normal post-surgical swelling
options.C: Encourage the patient to get out of bed and walk
options.D: Report the neurovascular changes to the physician immediately

explanation: Cool, pale toes with a sluggish refill mean blood flow is in trouble (or compartment syndrome is setting in). Always report this to the doctor right away!

question: What is the most crucial instruction for a patient taking a fast-acting sleeping pill?

options.A: Take the medication only when you are in bed and ready to sleep immediately
options.B: Wash down the pill with a glass of evening wine to enhance relaxation
options.C: Double your dose if you wake up in the middle of the night
options.D: Stop taking the medication abruptly after three days of use

explanation: These drugs work super fast! Patients must already be tucked in bed so they don't stagger around the ward and injure themselves.

question: Roughly what fraction of your total body water lives outside the cells (extracellular fluid)?

options.A: Three-quarters
options.B: One-half
options.C: Two-thirds
options.D: One-third

explanation: Spot on! About one-third of our body fluid flows outside the cells, while the other two-thirds stays safely inside. You've got this!

question: Which airway maneuver is safest to use when a neck injury is suspected?

options.A: Neck-hyperextension method
options.B: Rapid lateral neck rotation
options.C: Jaw-thrust maneuver
options.D: Head-tilt/chin-lift maneuver

explanation: The jaw-thrust maneuver opens the airway without moving or bending the cervical spine, protecting the patient from further spinal cord damage. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h3)

question: Why are nurses considered central to safe waste management in a hospital?

options.A: They purchase all the disposal bags and bins
options.B: They are legally required to transport waste off-site
options.C: They design the incinerators used for burning trash
options.D: They generate and dispose of medical waste daily

explanation: Nurses perform procedures like injections and dressing changes every day, meaning they make the first choices about where waste goes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h1)

question: An older adult suddenly reports muffled hearing in one ear. What simple cause should you check for first?

options.A: A ruptured tympanic membrane from aging
options.B: Permanent damage to the auditory nerve
options.C: Impacted earwax blocking the canal
options.D: Degeneration of the cochlear hair cells

explanation: Always look for the simplest, most treatable cause first! A buildup of earwax (cerumen) is super common and easy to fix.

question: When a nurse checks your reflexes and muscle movement, which part of the nervous system's job is being tested?

options.A: Motor output
options.B: Sensory adaptation
options.C: Chemical digestion
options.D: Hormonal secretion

explanation: You got this! Testing reflexes and muscle movement checks how well the nervous system sends signals out to effectors like muscles to create movement.

question: When is using a mucous membrane route (like sublingual or rectal) a lifesaver for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a subcutaneous injection
options.B: When the medication must bypass the skin entirely
options.C: When the patient is unable to swallow oral medications
options.D: When the drug requires slow digestion in the stomach

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is too weak, drowsy, or vomiting too much to swallow pills, routes like under the tongue or rectally keep their treatment going smoothly.

question: Why is delayed bathing recommended for stable newborns immediately after birth?

options.A: It allows the umbilical cord stump to dry
options.B: It helps preserve vernix for skin immunity
options.C: It prevents early neonatal jaundice spikes
options.D: It prevents rapid heat loss and cold stress

explanation: Washing a wet baby too soon strips away heat through evaporation, putting them at high risk for dangerous drops in body temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h4)

question: Why are engineering controls generally preferred over personal protective equipment?

options.A: They do not rely on the worker remembering to wear them correctly every day
options.B: They completely eliminate the hazard from the universe
options.C: They are the only legal requirement for hospitals
options.D: They cost nothing to install and maintain over time

explanation: Engineering controls work automatically in the background, reducing human error in safety maintenance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: You check a patient's vital signs before giving their scheduled beta-blocker. Which finding means you should hold the dose and check with the doctor?

options.A: Mild swelling in the lower ankles by evening
options.B: A resting heart rate of 50 beats per minute
options.C: A blood pressure reading of 120 over 80 mmHg
options.D: A slight complaint of daytime feeling sleepy

explanation: Beta-blockers slow the heart down. If the pulse drops below 60 beats per minute, that's bradycardia, and giving another dose could cause it to drop too low!

question: Why do traditional ideas of masculinity often cause men to delay getting medical care?

options.A: Fear of appearing weak prevents early reporting of symptoms
options.B: Biological factors make men immune to chronic illnesses
options.C: Men possess a higher natural threshold for all diseases
options.D: Hospitals routinely turn away male patients for checkups

explanation: Exactly. When society tells men they must always be tough and self-reliant, many fear that admitting pain or sickness makes them look weak.

question: Why must a nurse always use the exact liquid diluent provided by the manufacturer when mixing a powdered vaccine?

options.A: Using regular sterile water will cause the glass vial to shatter
options.B: Manufacturer diluents are flavored to reduce pediatric pain
options.C: Normal saline permanently stains the child's skin blue
options.D: The correct diluent ensures proper chemical balance and safety

explanation: Spot on! Mixing with the wrong fluid can ruin the vaccine or make it unsafe for the patient.

question: A community midwife visits a mother four days after delivery at home. What should be the primary focus of this visit?

options.A: Starting the baby on solid foods to boost early growth
options.B: Administering a complete set of adolescent reproductive counseling
options.C: Scheduling the mother for immediate return to work duties
options.D: Checking breastfeeding attachment, uterine involution, and lochia

explanation: Early postnatal visits prioritize assessing physical recovery, checking the uterus and lochia, and ensuring proper breastfeeding to prevent early complications. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h3)

question: What does the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) storage rule mean?

options.A: Using older food items before newer ones
options.B: Throwing away food on the first day of purchase
options.C: Cooking all food items on the same day
options.D: Placing new food items at the front of the shelf

explanation: FIFO ensures older stock is used first so nothing sits long enough to spoil or pass its expiration date. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h8)

question: Which symptom experienced immediately after the contrast injection is considered a normal, expected reaction?

options.A: Sudden swelling of the tongue and lips
options.B: Complete inability to speak or move
options.C: Severe shortness of breath and wheezing
options.D: A warm flushing sensation and a salty taste

explanation: Most patients feel a sudden wave of warmth and notice a metallic or salty taste when the dye enters their bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is it called when a patient with kidney failure has a dangerous buildup of potassium in their blood?

options.A: Hypercalcemia
options.B: Hyperkalemia
options.C: Hypoglycemia
options.D: Hyponatremia

explanation: Break the word down: 'hyper' means high, 'kalium' is the Latin root for potassium, and 'emia' means in the blood. When kidneys fail, they can't clear out potassium, leading to hyperkalemia.

question: What is the primary goal of providing quality care in reproductive health?

options.A: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions
options.B: Ensuring services are safe, effective, and respectful
options.C: Lowering the operational costs of the clinic
options.D: Maximizing the daily number of patients seen

explanation: Quality care focuses on delivering safe, effective, and respectful services that build client trust and promote positive health outcomes. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why must you check a baseline PTT before starting a patient on a heparin infusion?

options.A: To determine if the patient requires an emergency platelet transfusion
options.B: To calculate future dose adjustments safely against the patient's starting point
options.C: To prove the patient has never been exposed to anticoagulant medication
options.D: To check the patient's kidney function before drug administration begins

explanation: Everyone's blood clots a little differently. Knowing the patient's starting PTT helps you adjust their heparin drip safely without causing bleeding complications.

question: You hear gurgling sounds and see thick secretions in an unconscious patient's mouth. What is your very first action?

options.A: Turn the patient flat on their back and offer water
options.B: Administer a sleeping pill to calm the patient down
options.C: Wait for the doctor to arrive before doing anything
options.D: Suction the airway to clear out the secretions

explanation: Brilliant! Gurgling means the airway is blocked. Grab that suction machine right away to help them breathe easy again.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of a psychotic disorder like schizophrenia?

options.A: A break with reality including hallucinations
options.B: Fear of public speaking in large crowds
options.C: Impulsive spending habits during shopping
options.D: Extreme sadness lasting for only two days

explanation: Psychotic disorders involve losing touch with shared reality, which can show up as hearing or seeing things that aren't there (hallucinations) or strong fixed beliefs that aren't true (delusions).

question: Which common substance is often added to hot water in a Nelson inhaler to ease breathing?

options.A: Liquid paraffin wax
options.B: Intravenous saline
options.C: Tincture of benzoin
options.D: Hydrogen peroxide

explanation: Correct! Tincture of benzoin (or menthol) is a classic bedside additive that adds comforting, aromatic vapors to the steam.

question: Who represents a multidisciplinary team working together in a rural community setting?

options.A: Individual nurses working in complete isolation from peers
options.B: Only senior hospital physicians meeting in private offices
options.C: A group of patients waiting outside a closed pharmacy
options.D: Nurses, environmental health officers, and social workers

explanation: You've got this! Healthcare isn't a one-person show. Bringing nurses, sanitation officers, and social workers together ensures we tackle health problems from every angle.

question: What is the primary health benefit of a PTA providing a borehole in a school?

options.A: It lowers the electricity bills of the school
options.B: It provides mineral water for teachers to sell
options.C: It reduces the spread of waterborne diseases
options.D: It ensures students wash their uniforms daily

explanation: Clean and safe drinking water prevents dangerous waterborne infections such as typhoid and cholera among pupils. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the main job of our skin, hair, and nails (the integumentary system)?

options.A: Regulating red blood cell production in bone marrow
options.B: Facilitating conscious voluntary muscle movement
options.C: Synthesizing essential water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Protecting the body from environmental hazards

explanation: Think of your skin as your body's personal security guard! It is your first line of defense against germs, harsh chemicals, and physical injury.

question: What do we call the mature, fluid-filled follicle that is fully ready to release an egg?

options.A: Corpus albicans
options.B: Primordial follicle
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, mature stage before it bursts open to release the egg. Great landmark to remember in reproductive anatomy!

question: Which of these is a key advocacy role for a nurse working in a geriatric home?

options.A: Enforcing strict institutional routines without exception
options.B: Ensuring residents retain their dignity and rights
options.C: Making all financial decisions for the resident
options.D: Replacing family members during social visits

explanation: Nurses stand up for older adults to make sure their personal choices and human rights are always respected. You are their voice!

question: Which patients in a hospital setting require the use of standard precautions?

options.A: All patients regardless of their diagnosis
options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only patients who have open wounds
options.D: Only patients with confirmed infectious diseases

explanation: Standard precautions are designed for every patient interaction because infection status is not always known upon admission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why are infectious agents like Hepatitis B classified as cancer risk factors?

options.A: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body
options.B: They lower body temperature and stop normal digestion
options.C: They block the absorption of vital nutrients in the gut
options.D: They cause chronic inflammation and cellular damage over time

explanation: Certain viruses and bacteria lead to long-term tissue damage and inflammation, which increases the chance of cellular mutations. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the nurse's main job right after a tissue sample (biopsy) is taken?

options.A: Place the tissue sample in a household refrigerator until the morning shift
options.B: Examine the cells under the ward microscope to give an early report
options.C: Wash the specimen with sterile water to remove any residual blood
options.D: Ensure correct labeling and prompt placement in the proper preservative solution

explanation: Good lab results start with proper handling! Labeling it right away and putting it in the right preservative keeps the sample safe for testing.

question: After putting in an endotracheal tube, what is the quickest and most reliable bedside check to confirm it is in the right place?

options.A: Measuring the blood pressure
options.B: Checking chest expansion visually
options.C: End-tidal carbon dioxide detection
options.D: Listening to the stomach sounds

explanation: Carbon dioxide only comes out of the lungs! Finding CO2 right after the tube goes in proves it is sitting safely in the trachea and not accidentally down the esophagus.

question: What is a major safety concern when giving sleeping pills (sedative-hypnotics) to older adults?

options.A: Severe respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Increased risk of falls

explanation: Sleeping pills can cause daytime drowsiness and dizziness, making older adults unsteady on their feet and putting them at a high risk for accidental falls.

question: What happens when a drug that slows down liver enzymes is taken with another medication?

options.A: The second drug is excreted through the kidneys within minutes
options.B: The second drug binds more tightly to plasma proteins in the blood
options.C: The second drug breaks down slower, increasing the risk of toxicity
options.D: The second drug absorbs much faster from the stomach lining

explanation: If the liver's processing speed is slowed down, the companion drug hangs around longer instead of clearing out. Over time, it builds up in the blood to levels that can become toxic.

question: A patient with Parkinson's disease cannot swallow large pills, and their prescribed capsule is extended-release. What is the safest nursing action?

options.A: Crush the capsule into powder and mix it with food
options.B: Open the capsule and dissolve the beads in hot water
options.C: Consult the pharmacist or doctor for an alternative liquid or formulation
options.D: Skip the dose completely until their swallowing gets better

explanation: Spot on! Never crush extended-release medications because it ruins the special coating, causing all the medicine to flood the body at once and risking a dangerous overdose. Always talk to pharmacy!

question: A spouse is blocked from working and denied access to family money. What type of abuse is this?

options.A: Economic abuse
options.B: Psychological abuse
options.C: Traditional maltreatment
options.D: Physical violence

explanation: Exactly! Controlling someone's finances makes them financially dependent, which is a key tactic abusers use to trap victims.

question: Which of these is a direct positive patient outcome linked to having highly motivated nurses?

options.A: Higher frequency of disciplinary hearings for junior staff
options.B: Increased total cost of medical supplies per admission
options.C: Faster turnaround times for hospital building construction
options.D: Lower rates of hospital-acquired infections and patient falls

explanation: When nurses are motivated and alert, they pay close attention to safety checks, which directly protects patients from preventable slips, falls, and infections.

question: Which laboratory test is most commonly used to monitor a patient taking warfarin?

options.A: White blood cell differential
options.B: Total red blood cell count
options.C: Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time
options.D: Prothrombin Time and INR

explanation: Prothrombin Time and its standardized INR ratio are the standard tests used to track the effectiveness of warfarin therapy. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h7)

question: When does the postpartum period officially begin?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: Twenty-four hours after delivery
options.C: When the baby takes its first breath
options.D: At the start of labor

explanation: The postnatal period kicks off right after the third stage of labor when the placenta comes out. Simple and straightforward!

question: What is the main goal of Family Life Education in the community?

options.A: Promoting overall well-being and disease prevention
options.B: Treating acute medical and surgical emergencies
options.C: Managing chronic hospital admissions
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders in infants

explanation: Family Life Education is all about helping people stay healthy and preventing problems before they start, rather than treating emergencies.

question: Which clinical sign suggests that a newborn with a skull injury may have underlying intracranial pressure?

options.A: A strong grip reflex in both hands
options.B: Rapid passage of meconium stool
options.C: A high-pitched cry and lethargy
options.D: An intense craving for frequent feeds

explanation: Neurological irritability, altered levels of consciousness like lethargy, and a high-pitched cry are classic indicators of increased pressure inside the cranium. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h4)

question: What do we call a small drug molecule that joins with body proteins to trigger an immune response?

options.A: An antibody
options.B: An electrolyte
options.C: A hormone
options.D: A hapten

explanation: A hapten is like a tiny hitchhiker! It's too small on its own to bother the immune system, but once it attaches to a larger body protein, the immune system notices and reacts.

question: What is a key nursing responsibility when using continuous pulse oximetry on a hospitalized patient?

options.A: Leaving the same sensor taped to one finger for the entire week
options.B: Relying solely on the digital number without looking at the patient
options.C: Moving the sensor to a new site periodically to prevent skin breakdown
options.D: Turning off the audible alarm so patients can sleep peacefully

explanation: Continuous pressure from a sensor probe can damage fragile skin, so nurses must rotate the monitoring site regularly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the main way classic quinoline antimalarial drugs work?

options.A: Binding directly to human liver cell receptors
options.B: Destroying the nervous system of the mosquito vector
options.C: Preventing the detoxification of heme inside the parasite
options.D: Enhancing the production of red blood cells in bone marrow

explanation: Well done! As the parasite digests red blood cells, it releases toxic heme. Quinoline drugs stop the parasite from turning this heme into safe crystals, effectively poisoning it.

question: How does a rectal washout mostly differ from a regular cleansing enema?

options.A: It uses larger fluid volumes and cycles to thoroughly wash the lower colon
options.B: It is used exclusively to treat severe upper respiratory infections
options.C: It is only performed by surgeons in the operating theatre
options.D: It relies entirely on oral medications rather than rectal tubes

explanation: While a normal enema gives a quick flush, a rectal washout uses back-and-forth filling and draining cycles for a much deeper clean.

question: You just received a delivery of delicate protein medications for your ward. What is your very first priority?

options.A: Place the vials in a warm blanket warmer to activate them
options.B: Store them openly on the nurse's station desk for easy access
options.C: Crush the vials to prepare liquid doses for oral feeding tubes
options.D: Check and follow the required cold-chain refrigeration rules

explanation: Biotech protein drugs are super fragile! They'll lose their potency quickly if they aren't kept at the right cold temperature right away.

question: Why might a hospital find it hard to use primary nursing instead of team nursing?

options.A: Team nursing requires every single staff member to hold a master's degree.
options.B: Primary nursing completely eliminates the need for any communication with doctors.
options.C: Team nursing prevents nurses from ever talking to patients or families.
options.D: Primary nursing requires a larger proportion of registered nurses, which increases staffing costs.

explanation: Primary nursing needs lots of qualified Registered Nurses to give that individualized care, which can be expensive for hospital management compared to mixing in more junior staff.

question: How does incidence differ from prevalence in community health data?

options.A: Incidence counts deaths, while prevalence counts active infections
options.B: Incidence is calculated yearly, while prevalence is calculated daily
options.C: Incidence measures new cases over time, while prevalence measures total existing cases
options.D: Incidence only applies to children, while prevalence applies to adults

explanation: Incidence tracks how fast a disease is spreading by counting new cases, whereas prevalence shows how widespread a condition currently is within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why should nurses encourage patients to use adaptive tools during ADLs?

options.A: To promote maximum personal independence and self-esteem
options.B: To speed up morning routine times completely
options.C: To eliminate the need for any nursing supervision
options.D: To reduce the workload of the hospital laundry staff

explanation: Using tools like velcro or weighted spoons allows patients to complete tasks themselves, which builds confidence and preserves autonomy. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary chemical messenger released at the neuromuscular junction to cause muscle contraction?

options.A: Acetylcholine
options.B: Dopamine
options.C: Serotonin
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the key neurotransmitter stored in nerve terminals that crosses the synaptic cleft to stimulate muscle fiber receptors. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a 'root-cause analysis' when a mistake happens in a safe hospital?

options.A: Finding the exact junior staff member to blame for the incident
options.B: Writing a formal warning letter for the nurse's personal file
options.C: Examining the underlying system failures that allowed the error to happen
options.D: Deciding how much money the hospital should fine the ward

explanation: Instead of pointing fingers at a person, root-cause analysis looks at what went wrong in the system (like equipment or communication) so it never happens again.

question: Why do large arteries possess thick walls rich in elastic tissue?

options.A: To allow rapid diffusion of oxygen and carbon dioxide across the vessel wall
options.B: To store extra white blood cells during a systemic bacterial infection
options.C: To trap blood clots before they reach smaller vessels in the brain
options.D: To withstand and buffer the high-pressure surges of blood coming directly from the heart

explanation: The high elasticity of large arteries helps them absorb the forceful pulses of blood pumped by the heart, smoothing out pressure fluctuations. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: How should you position your patient's head during an eye wash?

options.A: Tilted slightly toward the affected side
options.B: Tilted firmly toward the unaffected side
options.C: Positioned flat and facing straight up
options.D: Tilted backward as far as the neck allows

explanation: Tilting toward the bad side ensures the dirty runoff flows away off the face instead of spilling into the healthy eye.

question: Why might a very stressed or anxious mum find it hard to express milk?

options.A: Stress permanently destroys the lactiferous ducts inside the breast
options.B: Anxiety causes the anterior pituitary to completely stop making prolactin
options.C: Nerve impulses from the nipple travel backward during panic attacks
options.D: Adrenaline constricts blood vessels and interferes with oxytocin release

explanation: You're doing great! Stress releases adrenaline, which gets in the way of oxytocin and makes the milk harder to let down. Relaxation is key!

question: A patient with a mild viral cold is given three different strong antibiotics. What does this show?

options.A: The ideal use of the National Essential Medicines List
options.B: Irrational prescribing and potential misuse of drugs
options.C: An excellent example of standard clinical protocol
options.D: A necessary step to prevent common tropical diseases

explanation: Antibiotics don't cure viruses! Giving them unnecessarily is a classic example of drug misuse that we want to avoid.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to encourage a traumatized widow to share her story?

options.A: Threatening to report her family to the police immediately
options.B: Insisting that she discuss the traumatic details in a crowded ward
options.C: Building trust through empathetic and confidential communication
options.D: Ignoring the emotional state and focusing only on vital signs

explanation: Patients who have been mistreated need a safe, private, and non-judgmental space before they can open up. Your kindness makes all the difference.

question: Which sign tells you a newborn has latched on correctly for breastfeeding?

options.A: The infant's lips are flanged outward covering much of the areola
options.B: The infant remains completely silent with eyes tightly closed
options.C: The mother feels a sharp pinching sensation during active sucking
options.D: The baby sucks only on the protruding tip of the nipple

explanation: A wide, open latch with lips flared out over a good chunk of the areola means the baby gets enough milk and mum won't end up with cracked, sore nipples.

question: Why does joint looseness during pregnancy make women more prone to muscle or joint injury?

options.A: It causes rapid and uncontrolled bone growth in limbs.
options.B: It reduces joint stability across the entire skeletal system.
options.C: It stops bones from absorbing necessary dietary calcium.
options.D: It decreases the overall strength of muscle fibers.

explanation: When ligaments become loose, joints lose their normal tight support. This makes them much more prone to strain and injury during everyday tasks. You've got this!

question: How do organophosphate poisons mess with the nervous system?

options.A: By blocking acetylcholinesterase and causing neurotransmitter accumulation
options.B: By drying up all bodily fluids through immediate kidney failure
options.C: By turning the blood acidic within seconds of skin contact
options.D: By freezing the spinal cord to completely stop all nerve impulses

explanation: That's right! They block the enzyme that normally cleans up acetylcholine, meaning nerves keep firing continuously without a break.

question: Why does widespread use of antibiotics naturally lead to more resistant germs?

options.A: Drugs cause healthy human cells to mutate into resistant bacteria
options.B: Pathogens learn to consume the antibiotic drugs as a primary food source
options.C: Medicines expire quickly in tropical climates and lose their potency
options.D: Surviving microbes pass on their protective traits to the next generation

explanation: Think of it like survival of the fittest. When weak germs are killed off, the tough ones left behind breed and pass on their protective superpowers to their offspring! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T92#GNS214_U1_T92_h1)

question: Through which openings does cerebrospinal fluid leave the fourth ventricle to flow around the outside of the brain?

options.A: Internal carotid canals
options.B: Cerebral aqueduct channels
options.C: Median and lateral apertures
options.D: Interventricular foramina

explanation: Well done! The median and lateral apertures act like exit doors in the fourth ventricle, letting fluid flow out into the subarachnoid space.

question: A patient asks about the tough, fibrous outer sheath covering the erectile tissue of the penis. What is it called?

options.A: Tunica albuginea
options.B: Perineal membrane
options.C: Dartos fascia
options.D: Scrotal septum

explanation: The tunica albuginea is a strong, protective jacket of connective tissue that holds everything firmly in place during an erection.

question: Which nursing action helps build instant trust with a newly admitted PAC patient?

options.A: Reviewing the client's chart at the nursing station before entering
options.B: Asking the client to sign financial clearance forms immediately
options.C: Instructing visitors to leave the ward before nursing assessment begins
options.D: Explaining every clinical procedure clearly before touching the client

explanation: Telling her what you are about to do shows deep respect for her body and eases the fear of feeling helpless in the hospital.

question: What is the main difference between measurement and evaluation in nursing school?

options.A: Measurement is done by students, while evaluation is done strictly by hospital managers.
options.B: Measurement assigns numbers, while evaluation interprets those numbers to make a judgment.
options.C: Measurement evaluates clinical skills, while evaluation tests written knowledge.
options.D: Measurement focuses on attitudes, while evaluation focuses purely on psychomotor tasks.

explanation: Think of measurement as gathering raw data like your test score (e.g., 75%), while evaluation decides what that score actually means for your progress as a nurse. You've got this!

question: Why is spotting a specific 'toxidrome' (group of symptoms) so helpful in emergency care?

options.A: It proves legal liability for workplace safety violations
options.B: It stops the chemical from absorbing through unbroken skin
options.C: It guides rapid clinical management before lab tests confirm the toxin
options.D: It eliminates the need to decontaminate the patient's clothing

explanation: Lab tests take time! Spotting a familiar pattern of symptoms lets you start life-saving antidotes and care right away.

question: Why is mouth care seen as a core nursing duty rather than just making a patient look neat?

options.A: Hospital rules state that nurses must inspect teeth every morning
options.B: Dentists are almost never found inside general hospital wards
options.C: The mouth is a main doorway for germs to enter the rest of the body
options.D: Being sick always makes patients completely lose their sense of taste

explanation: Spot on! The mouth opens directly into our breathing and digestive pipes, meaning good oral care protects the whole body, not just the teeth.

question: Which of these is NOT a common fetal complication linked to untreated hyperemesis?

options.A: Intestinal growth restriction
options.B: Low birth weight
options.C: Congenital heart murmurs
options.D: Preterm birth

explanation: Heart defects happen during early structural development, whereas hyperemesis baby issues are usually about poor nutrition and low birth weight. You're mastering neonatal risks!

question: Which chemical messenger do anticholinergic drugs block in the bladder?

options.A: Dopamine
options.B: Serotonin
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Think of acetylcholine as the trigger messenger. Anticholinergics block it from binding to receptors, preventing unwanted muscle squeezes.

question: Which feature is typical of a benign tumor?

options.A: It destroys neighboring healthy organs
options.B: It is enclosed by a fibrous capsule
options.C: It looks completely different from normal cells
options.D: It spreads quickly through the bloodstream

explanation: Benign growths typically form a distinct capsule that separates them from surrounding tissue, making them easier to excise. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h2)

question: The neural tube, which forms the brain and spinal cord, develops from which germ layer?

options.A: Endoderm
options.B: Trophoblast
options.C: Mesoderm
options.D: Ectoderm

explanation: Since the nervous system links closely with the skin and outer structures, it comes right from the ectoderm layer. Excellent recall!

question: What is the most life-threatening type of bleeding that can happen to someone with a severe bleeding disorder?

options.A: Intracranial hemorrhage
options.B: Epistaxis from the nose
options.C: Petechiae on the skin
options.D: Gingival bleeding while brushing

explanation: Bleeding inside the skull (intracranial hemorrhage) puts heavy pressure on the brain. It can cause rapid confusion, unconsciousness, or worse if nurses don't catch it early.

question: Why do standard health programs sometimes fail when trying to help marginalized groups?

options.A: They focus exclusively on wealthy urban business owners
options.B: They are always illegal under Nigerian state legislation
options.C: They often ignore specific social and economic barriers faced by those groups
options.D: They require patients to hold international passports

explanation: A one-size-fits-all approach often misses the unique financial, cultural, or physical hurdles that vulnerable people face every day.

question: A patient complains of chest pain and trouble swallowing because their food pipe is squeezing in an uncoordinated way. What is this called?

options.A: Oesophageal varices
options.B: Hiatus hernia
options.C: Oesophageal spasm
options.D: Mallory-Weiss tear

explanation: Correct! When the muscles of the oesophagus contract in a chaotic, painful squeeze rather than smooth waves, it's called an oesophageal spasm.

question: What is the main focus of primordial prevention?

options.A: Rehabilitating patients after a stroke
options.B: Treating acute symptoms in a hospital ward
options.C: Broad social and environmental policies
options.D: Screening high-risk groups for hidden diseases

explanation: Primordial prevention tackles the root societal and environmental conditions that create health risks before they even start. You've got this!

question: Why do nurses check oxygen levels (pulse oximetry) on both a newborn's right hand and their feet?

options.A: To confirm that the umbilical cord was clamped in the correct location
options.B: To compare pre-ductal and post-ductal oxygen levels for abnormal shunting
options.C: To measure how fast blood is traveling through the ductus venosus
options.D: To ensure the liver is receiving enough blood through the hepatic portal system

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! The right hand gets blood before the ductus arteriosus shortcut, while the feet get blood after it. Comparing them helps nurses catch hidden heart issues early.

question: Which hormone signals the Leydig cells in the testes to make testosterone?

options.A: Luteinizing hormone (LH)
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH)
options.D: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA)

explanation: You've got this! Luteinizing hormone (LH) travels from the brain's pituitary gland down to the testes, giving the green light for testosterone production.

question: Why is patient coercion a serious worry during research recruitment?

options.A: Ethical boards do not allow patients to receive free medication
options.B: Coerced patients always give false answers on questionnaires
options.C: Patients might feel forced to join because their nurse or doctor asked
options.D: Hospital management requires a 100 percent recruitment rate

explanation: Brilliant! Patients respect their nurses and doctors so much that they might fear getting bad care if they say 'no,' which makes true voluntary consent tricky.

question: A young female client has extra facial hair, acne, and irregular periods. Which condition matches these signs?

options.A: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.B: Primary amenorrhea
options.C: Endometriosis
options.D: Pelvic organ prolapse

explanation: Great job! PCOS involves high male hormone levels (androgens), leading to signs like unwanted hair growth, acne, and irregular monthly cycles.

question: A community nurse is advising Nigerian mothers on affordable toddler meals. Which approach works best?

options.A: Tell mothers to avoid local vegetables because they lack minerals
options.B: Encourage combining local staples like beans and grains to make balanced meals
options.C: Insist that only imported tinned foods provide enough vitamins for growth
options.D: Advise mothers to feed the child only once a day with a large heavy meal

explanation: Brilliant! Using affordable local foods like beans and maize is sustainable, cost-effective, and keeps our little ones well-nourished.

question: Why are animal bite wounds often left open at first instead of being stitched up right away?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to apply daily bandages
options.B: To prevent trapping bacteria and reducing the risk of deep infection
options.C: To let the underlying bone heal before skin closure
options.D: To allow the skin to grow back faster without scarring

explanation: If you stitch up a dirty bite right away, you trap nasty bacteria inside. Leaving it open helps prevent painful abscesses.

question: When washing hands as a food handler, how long should you scrub with soap and water?

options.A: At least twenty seconds
options.B: Until they feel completely dry
options.C: Exactly five seconds
options.D: About two minutes

explanation: Good hygiene is our best shield! Scrubbing with soap for at least twenty seconds gives the soap enough time to lift away and destroy harmful germs.

question: Which group has the most influence over traditional community practices concerning marriage?

options.A: Commercial banking executives
options.B: Traditional and religious leaders
options.C: International tourism boards
options.D: Foreign economic advisors

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders hold deep respect and authority in local communities, making their involvement key to changing harmful cultural practices.

question: A patient has sharp, severe tummy pain that hurts much worse when they move or take a deep breath. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Irritation of the parietal peritoneum
options.B: Slow movement in the large bowel
options.C: Normal gas movement through the colon
options.D: Stretching of a hollow organ muscle

explanation: The parietal peritoneum has lots of somatic nerve fibers that react sharply to movement and inflammation, causing that localized, sharp pain.

question: If a patient is given a new drug classed as an antihypertensive, what main effect should you expect?

options.A: Elevated blood glucose
options.B: Reduced joint inflammation
options.C: Increased bacterial cell death
options.D: Lowered blood pressure

explanation: Well done! 'Anti' means against, and 'hypertensive' refers to high blood pressure—so antihypertensives bring high blood pressure down.

question: Why must insulin be given as an injection instead of swallowing it as a pill?

options.A: Injections allow insulin to bypass the liver entirely
options.B: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the insulin molecule
options.C: Stomach acid turns insulin into a toxic compound
options.D: Oral pills are absorbed too rapidly to be safe

explanation: Exactly! Insulin is a protein, so the acids and enzymes in your gut would break it down before it ever reached your bloodstream if you swallowed it.

question: What does truly comprehensive Post-Abortion Care (PAC) involve beyond treating medical emergencies?

options.A: Restricting her fluid intake to monitor kidney output
options.B: Providing emotional support and linking her to family planning services
options.C: Reporting her to local law enforcement authorities
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately without speaking to her

explanation: Spot on! PAC isn't just about patching up physical injuries; it's caring for her mental well-being and future reproductive health too.

question: Why is it usually unhelpful to just punish a nurse after a mistake happens on the ward?

options.A: It stops other staff members from documenting patient care properly
options.B: It ignores the underlying system flaws that allowed the error to happen
options.C: It makes the nurse work faster during the next emergency shift
options.D: It increases the budget available for buying new medical equipment

explanation: Exactly! Blaming just one person doesn't fix a broken system. To keep patients safe, we have to fix the root causes so the same mistake doesn't happen again.

question: Where should you position the lower edge of the blood pressure cuff on the patient's arm?

options.A: About one inch above the inner elbow crease
options.B: Right up against the shoulder joint
options.C: Directly over the bony wrist
options.D: Halfway down the forearm

explanation: Placing it about an inch above the elbow crease ensures the inner bladder sits right over the brachial artery. Perfect placement!

question: Which Nigerian law specifically tackles harmful traditional practices and gender-based violence?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: Criminal Code for Corporate Fraud
options.D: Standard Environmental Sanitation Decree

explanation: The VAPP Act gives law enforcement a legal tool to protect people from physical, emotional, and traditional abuse, including harmful widowhood practices.

question: What physical event causes a sudden rise in the newborn's systemic blood pressure?

options.A: Clamping of the umbilical cord
options.B: The baby crying for the first time
options.C: Closure of the foramen ovale
options.D: Contraction of the ductus arteriosus

explanation: Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which sharply increases resistance and pressure in the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: What tiny muscle attached to hair follicles pulls hair upright to give us goosebumps?

options.A: Sebaceous muscle
options.B: Matrix fiber
options.C: Arrector pili
options.D: Keratin strand

explanation: You nailed it! The arrector pili is a tiny smooth muscle that contracts when we're cold or scared, pulling our hair follicles straight up.

question: Which nursing diagnosis is most appropriate for a patient suffering from constant urine leakage caused by a fistula?

options.A: Risk for infection
options.B: Ineffective airway clearance
options.C: Impaired physical mobility
options.D: Deficient fluid volume

explanation: Constant exposure to urine on the perineal skin creates a very high risk for localized skin breakdown and severe infection. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h5)

question: Which equipment design helps lower the chance of a spinal headache?

options.A: Atraumatic pencil-point needles
options.B: Wide-bore metal needles
options.C: Disposable plastic syringes
options.D: Flexible silicone tubing

explanation: Correct! Pencil-point needles gently push fibers aside instead of cutting them, allowing the puncture hole to seal much faster.

question: How is cancer grading different from cancer staging?

options.A: Grading counts white blood cells, while staging counts red blood cells
options.B: Grading is only used for benign tumors, while staging is for malignant ones
options.C: Grading looks at cellular appearance under a microscope, while staging looks at how far the cancer has spread
options.D: Grading measures organ failure, while staging measures treatment success

explanation: Think of it this way: Grading checks how 'wild' or abnormal the cells look under a microscope, while staging looks at the map of the body to see how far the cancer has traveled.

question: How do case studies mainly help nursing students build real-world competence?

options.A: By teaching them how to repair broken hospital equipment
options.B: By replacing all hospital ward practicals with computer games
options.C: By forcing them to memorize long lists of medical terminology
options.D: By challenging them to analyze real patient situations and plan care

explanation: Case studies bridge that gap between boring textbook theory and the actual ward by letting you think through real patient scenarios.

question: What is the most important daily habit for preventing foot complications in a patient with nerve loss?

options.A: Inspecting the feet daily for cuts, blisters, and pressure injuries
options.B: Encouraging barefoot walking indoors to stimulate deep tendon reflexes
options.C: Massaging the toes vigorously with alcohol twice a day
options.D: Applying high-strength heating pads to the calves every evening

explanation: When you can't feel your feet, small cuts can turn into big, infected sores without you noticing. Daily checks catch little problems before they become emergencies!

question: What are the classic early signs someone might show when developing new type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Painful joints in the hands and feet
options.B: Sudden swelling in both lower legs
options.C: Excessive thirst and frequent urination
options.D: Yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes

explanation: Spot on! When blood sugar is too high, the body pulls water into the urine to flush it out, leaving the patient super thirsty and running to the toilet constantly.

question: Why does adjusting to a dark room take much longer than adjusting to bright light?

options.A: Rod pigments take time to regenerate in the dark
options.B: Blood flow to the retina stops temporarily
options.C: The pupil takes hours to dilate fully
options.D: The cornea must change its thickness overnight

explanation: Your eye's light-sensitive chemicals take a little while to rebuild after being bleached by light. Patience is key, both in exams and in learning!

question: Which method of applying a painful stimulus is usually avoided in modern nursing because it causes unnecessary bruising?

options.A: Supraorbital pressure
options.B: Trapezius squeeze
options.C: Nail bed pressure
options.D: Sternal rub

explanation: Vigorous sternal rubbing (grinding knuckles on the chest bone) can leave nasty bruises and trauma. Safer methods like a trapezius squeeze are preferred today.

question: Why is taking a nighttime dose of a cystine-binding medication so important?

options.A: Cystine excretion often peaks at night during periods of sleep and dehydration
options.B: Kidney blood flow drops to zero during deep sleep, requiring higher drug levels
options.C: Bedtime dosing completely eliminates the need for daytime water intake
options.D: The liver metabolizes the medication much faster during daylight hours

explanation: At night, we sleep without drinking water, making our urine concentrated. A bedtime dose protects the kidneys during those vulnerable overnight hours!

question: How does teaching lifestyle habits help a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It cures the genetic condition entirely through proper daily nutrition and rest
options.B: It guarantees that they will never experience chronic fatigue or joint pain again
options.C: It teaches them how to safely perform their own blood transfusions at home
options.D: It helps them avoid common triggers like dehydration and extreme cold to prevent crises

explanation: Knowledge is power! When patients know what sets off a crisis—like staying hydrated or dressing warmly—they can take charge of their daily health and stay out of the hospital.

question: What exactly is colostrum?

options.A: The thick, yellowish first breast milk produced after birth
options.B: The primary protein supplement used to treat severe malnutrition
options.C: A local porridge made from fermented yellow maize
options.D: A traditional herbal drink given to calm crying babies

explanation: Colostrum is the super-nutritious, antibody-rich milk that comes right after delivery. Sadly, bad taboos sometimes cause mothers to throw it away—good thing you know better!

question: Why must oxygen delivery tubing be moved away before delivering a shock?

options.A: To keep the plastic tubing from melting onto the chest skin
options.B: To allow space for placing the defibrillator pads correctly
options.C: To stop the patient from breathing too much room air
options.D: To prevent electrical sparks from igniting an oxygen-rich fire

explanation: Oxygen feeds fire! Combining an electrical spark from a defibrillator pad with a high concentration of oxygen right near the chest is a major fire hazard.

question: What does a grating or crackling sound felt over a moving joint indicate?

options.A: Crepitus
options.B: Spasticity
options.C: Atrophy
options.D: Clonus

explanation: Crepitus happens when damaged joint surfaces or rough bone ends rub against each other during movement. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h4)

question: What happens to the physical size of the pituitary gland during pregnancy?

options.A: It moves to the abdomen
options.B: It enlarges
options.C: It stops working
options.D: It shrinks by half

explanation: Correct! Because it has to pump out way more hormones to support the pregnancy, the pituitary gland actually increases in size.

question: Which structures should you palpate when doing a routine male genital check?

options.A: Testes and epididymis
options.B: Bulbourethral glands only
options.C: Ureters and renal pelvis
options.D: Seminal vesicles and bladder

explanation: You got it! Gently checking the testes and the epididymis helps you spot any lumps, swelling, or tenderness early on.

question: A community needs a ward-level facility that can handle 24-hour deliveries and minor procedures. Which one should they use?

options.A: Mobile immunization clinic
options.B: Traditional birth attendant post
options.C: Primary Health Centre
options.D: Health Post

explanation: The Primary Health Centre (PHC) serves as the bigger hub at the ward headquarters, fully equipped for round-the-clock deliveries and minor treatments.

question: A patient needs a very early pregnancy test using urine. Which sample should you tell her to collect?

options.A: First morning urine
options.B: Timed two-hour urine
options.C: Random afternoon urine
options.D: Post-exercise urine

explanation: First morning urine is the most concentrated, meaning any early pregnancy hormones will be nice and strong and easy for the test to pick up!

question: What type of protective equipment is recommended when working with harsh chemical disinfectants that might splash?

options.A: Paper surgical caps and cloth masks
options.B: Open sandals and thin cotton gowns
options.C: Sterile surgical gloves and boots
options.D: Face shields and waterproof aprons

explanation: Face shields protect the eyes and mucous membranes from chemical splashes, while waterproof aprons protect clothing and skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of organophosphate (insecticide) poisoning?

options.A: Urinary incontinence
options.B: Extreme dryness of the skin
options.C: Watery eyes and diarrhea
options.D: Excessive salivation

explanation: Organophosphates throw the body's moisture switch into overdrive! Think watery eyes, drooling, and sweat—so the skin is definitely wet, never dry.

question: Why are nurses considered the frontline defense in pharmacovigilance?

options.A: They hold the legal authority to withdraw dangerous drugs from the market
options.B: They manufacture the pharmaceutical products used in hospital wards
options.C: They administer medications directly and observe patient reactions continuously
options.D: They write the clinical guidelines for pharmaceutical companies

explanation: That's right! Because we give the meds and spend the most time by the bedside, nurses are in the absolute best spot to catch early warning signs.

question: Why is it so important to start ORT early when a patient has acute diarrhea?

options.A: It stimulates the appetite for solid foods
options.B: It immediately kills the bacteria in the gut
options.C: It coats the intestinal lining to prevent pain
options.D: It prevents rapid progression to hypovolemic shock

explanation: Catching fluid loss early stops the body's fluid levels from dropping to dangerously low levels that can lead to shock and organ failure.

question: What simple bedside test is routinely done along with a blood count for fevers in malaria zones?

options.A: A fasting cholesterol check
options.B: A bone marrow test
options.C: A malaria rapid diagnostic test
options.D: A liver tissue biopsy

explanation: Great! Quick malaria tests and blood smears are our frontline tools for fast diagnoses.

question: What is the job of the air inlet on a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It locks the cork lid tightly into the ceramic jar
options.B: It lets the nurse pour medicine in while treating
options.C: It acts as a drain for extra water collection
options.D: It allows fresh air to mix with the rising steam

explanation: Exactly! The air inlet lets a bit of cooler room air mix with the vapor. This keeps the steam from being too scorching hot for the patient's mouth and throat.

question: What is the main focus of Behavioral Change Communication (BCC) in nutrition?

options.A: Addressing cultural habits and beliefs influencing food choices
options.B: Importing expensive nutritional supplements from abroad
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties for poor dietary habits
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on food chemical safety

explanation: That's right! BCC looks past simple facts to understand the cultural and social reasons behind how people choose and prepare their meals.

question: Why does a hospital ward have separate clean utility and dirty utility rooms?

options.A: To comply with fire safety evacuation rules
options.B: To give nurses a private space to take meal breaks
options.C: To separate male patients from female patients
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination between sterile supplies and waste

explanation: Separation ensures clean medical supplies do not mix with used equipment, body fluids, or waste items. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of the three tiny bones in the middle ear?

options.A: Produce cerumen to trap foreign bodies
options.B: Amplify and transmit sound vibrations
options.C: Drain excess fluid from the inner ear
options.D: Maintain balance and body posture

explanation: Meet the malleus, incus, and stapes! They take the vibrations from your eardrum, boost their volume, and pass them deeper into the ear.

question: Which type of control is used BEFORE patient care activities actually begin?

options.A: Concurrent control
options.B: Feedforward control
options.C: Feedback control
options.D: Retrospective control

explanation: Feedforward control is all about prevention—checking staff qualifications, equipment, and supplies before any patient care starts.

question: What is the best way for nurses to physically handle needles during a count?

options.A: Glance quickly over the tray from a distance
options.B: Count only the full packs without opening them
options.C: Let the surgeon handle the items alone
options.D: Point to or touch each item individually as it is counted
