question: Why should clinical nurses care about basic healthcare finance?

options.A: It ensures that nurses can perform formal yearly financial audits independently.
options.B: It helps them calculate and distribute monthly paychecks for all hospital staff.
options.C: It allows them to connect daily bedside care decisions to the financial health of the unit.
options.D: It removes the need for hospital administrators to monitor equipment purchases.

explanation: Every time you use supplies wisely or manage your shift without unnecessary overtime, you're helping your ward stay financially healthy and ready for patients!

question: What is the main job of a Governing Board in a public health corporation?

options.A: Providing direct bedside nursing care to patients
options.B: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs locally
options.C: Setting broad policy and overseeing financial management
options.D: Writing international health treaties

explanation: Well done! The board doesn't do bedside nursing; instead, they steer the ship by setting big goals and making sure finances are properly managed.

question: How do the fallopian tubes move an egg toward the uterus?

options.A: Using tiny waving cilia and smooth muscle contractions
options.B: By producing strong chemical suction currents
options.C: Using pulsating pressure from nearby arterial blood flow
options.D: Through rapid gravity shifts in the pelvic cavity

explanation: Correct! Tiny hair-like cilia wave back and forth while the tube muscles gently push the egg along on its journey.

question: A restless patient keeps scratching their skin. Why should you trim their nails right away?

options.A: To prevent broken skin and secondary infections
options.B: To increase blood flow to the fingertips
options.C: To help the patient sleep through the night
options.D: To stop the patient from feeling itchy altogether

explanation: Exactly. Trimming gets rid of sharp edges so that even if the patient scratches, they won't tear their skin open and invite in new infections.

question: What is the main job of a drug antagonist?

options.A: To block receptors and prevent activation
options.B: To speed up the breakdown of cellular waste
options.C: To mimic hormones and cause a strong response
options.D: To increase the rate of drug absorption

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a stubborn security guard standing in the doorway—it sits on the receptor so nothing else can trigger it.

question: Why do doctors often add co-analgesics to a patient's treatment plan?

options.A: To cause immediate unconsciousness during surgical procedures
options.B: To speed up the physical healing of broken bones and fractures
options.C: To replace all nursing physical assessments of comfort levels
options.D: To target specific pain types and reduce opioid requirements

explanation: By teaming up different types of pain meds, we can tackle stubborn pain better and use lower, safer doses of heavy opioids.

question: How does oxygen primarily travel through the bloodstream to body tissues?

options.A: Attached directly to white blood cells
options.B: Floating freely as pure gas bubbles in plasma
options.C: Bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells
options.D: Dissolved completely in blood platelets

explanation: The vast majority of oxygen in the body is carried by binding to the hemoglobin molecules inside red blood cells. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary action of a bacteriostatic antibiotic?

options.A: Instantly dissolving the cell wall of all viruses
options.B: Stopping the reproduction and growth of bacteria
options.C: Lowering the patient's fever by acting on the brain
options.D: Stimulating the patient's bone marrow to make platelets

explanation: Bacteriostatic drugs hit the pause button on bacterial multiplication so the body's natural immune system can easily finish clearing them out.

question: When is a doctor or lab scientist most likely to order a peripheral blood smear along with a regular full blood count?

options.A: As a quick kidney check before surgery
options.B: To check how much iron the patient eats over time
options.C: When the standard blood count shows unexpected results
options.D: To replace measuring total haemoglobin

explanation: A blood smear lets the lab actually look at the cells under a microscope when the numbers on the regular blood test look a bit strange.

question: If a category takes up 50 percent of your survey data, how many degrees should its slice be?

options.A: 180 degrees
options.B: 360 degrees
options.C: 45 degrees
options.D: 90 degrees

explanation: Well done! Since 50 percent is half, its slice has to be half of 360 degrees, which is 180 degrees.

question: Which main nerve links the gastrointestinal tract directly to the brain?

options.A: The phrenic nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The vagus nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary communication highway connecting your gut and your brain.

question: What is the primary purpose of inserting an endotracheal tube?

options.A: To secure and maintain a patent airway
options.B: To measure systemic blood pressure continuously
options.C: To prevent the stomach from producing acid
options.D: To treat underlying lung infections directly

explanation: The main goal of endotracheal intubation is to keep the airway open and secure so oxygen can reach the lungs safely. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the special component in fungal cell membranes that antifungal drugs love to target?

options.A: Cellulose
options.B: Peptidoglycan
options.C: Cholesterol
options.D: Ergosterol

explanation: Fungi use ergosterol in their cell membranes (while humans use cholesterol). This difference lets antifungal drugs attack the fungus without harming human cells!

question: What is the main job of the ascending nerve tracts passing through the brain stem?

options.A: Coordinating balance with the cerebellum
options.B: Carrying sensory signals up to the brain
options.C: Producing automatic breathing rhythms
options.D: Transmitting motor orders down to muscles

explanation: Remember that 'ascending' means going up! These tracts carry sensory information from your body all the way up to higher brain areas.

question: What is the main difference between primary and acquired immune deficiencies?

options.A: Primary deficiencies are always mild, while acquired deficiencies are fatal.
options.B: Primary deficiencies are present at birth, while acquired deficiencies develop later in life.
options.C: Acquired deficiencies can be cured with vitamins, but primary deficiencies cannot.
options.D: Primary deficiencies affect only red blood cells, while acquired deficiencies affect white cells.

explanation: Spot on! Primary immune conditions are inherited and present right from birth, whereas acquired ones happen due to outside factors later in life.

question: In a court of law, how is a patient's medical record treated?

options.A: As an optional personal diary
options.B: As a legally binding document
options.C: As temporary administrative notes
options.D: As a draft of medical opinions

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps.

question: Why are bronchodilators sometimes given along with antibiotics for a lung infection?

options.A: To dry up all fluid inside the chest cavity
options.B: To bring down the patient's fever
options.C: To directly kill the bacteria in the air sacs
options.D: To relax tight airways and make breathing easier

explanation: Bronchodilators relax the muscles around the breathing tubes, opening them up so air flows more smoothly.

question: What is the most crucial assessment for a nurse to do regularly on a limb with a tumor or post-op reconstruction?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity and pupillary light reflex
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the chest wall every hour
options.C: Neurovascular checks for pulse, color, movement, and sensation
options.D: Auscultating bowel sounds in all four abdominal quadrants

explanation: Swelling or tumor growth can squeeze blood vessels and nerves. Regular checks help us catch circulation issues early and protect the limb!

question: A patient with severe nephrotic syndrome is most likely to report which initial pattern of swelling?

options.A: Severe swelling limited to the toes
options.B: Sudden swelling of only the right hand
options.C: Puffiness around the eyes upon waking up
options.D: Throbbing pain and swelling in the jaw

question: What instruction should you give your patient right before you pull out an NG tube?

options.A: Breathe in and out through your mouth very fast
options.B: Suck on a hard candy immediately
options.C: Take a deep breath and hold it
options.D: Cough as hard as you can

question: How should a nurse respectfully address an older adult resident in Nigeria?

options.A: Using numbers assigned to their room beds
options.B: Using respectful honorific titles and polite language
options.C: By their first name to encourage casual friendliness
options.D: By referring to their specific medical diagnosis

explanation: Exactly! In our culture, showing respect to elders through proper titles like 'Mama', 'Papa', or respectful greetings goes a long way.

question: You receive a transcribed drug order with blurry handwriting and an old shorthand symbol. What is your best next step?

options.A: Ask another student nurse to guess what the symbol might mean
options.B: Wait until the patient's shift ends and let the next nurse handle it
options.C: Ask the prescribing clinician to clarify the order before administration
options.D: Administer the lowest possible dose listed in the pharmacy manual

explanation: You got it! When handwriting is blurry or abbreviations are confusing, always go straight to the prescriber to get clear instructions. Patient safety is always number one.

question: What is the main job of sodium fluoride inside the blood collection tube?

options.A: It stains white blood cells for the microscope
options.B: It speeds up blood clotting so serum separates instantly
options.C: It stops blood cells from consuming the glucose inside the tube
options.D: It stops the blood sample from freezing during transport

question: What is a major safety worry when giving hypnotic medications to elderly patients?

options.A: Sudden permanent blindness upon waking
options.B: Falls resulting from daytime drowsiness and dizziness
options.C: Rapid development of severe bone fractures
options.D: Permanent loss of long-term childhood memories

explanation: Older adults can feel 'hangover' drowsiness the next day, which makes them super unsteady on their feet and prone to nasty falls.

question: Why must we encourage patients to drink plenty of water right after a barium meal?

options.C: To dissolve any leftover barium remaining in the stomach

question: Why is it important to match your physical assessment clues with lab hormone test results?

options.D: To eliminate the need for ongoing vital sign monitoring

explanation: Lab numbers tell one part of the story, and what you see with your own eyes tells the rest. Putting them together helps you see if the treatment plan is actually working.

question: What is the main use of an oxygen tent in children's wards?

options.A: Administering aerosolized chemotherapy drugs

options.C: Delivering controlled oxygen in pediatric care
options.D: Treating severe burn wounds in sterile isolation

question: In Nigeria, which level of government is primarily responsible for running Primary Health Care (PHC) centers?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Defence
options.B: Private pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Local Government Council
options.D: International Health Organizations

explanation: Spot on! Primary Health Care in Nigeria is managed closely at the grassroots level by Local Government Councils.

question: What happens inside your chest when your diaphragm contracts to take in a normal breath?

options.A: Surface tension increases to make the lung tissue stiffer
options.B: Intrapleural pressure decreases to draw air into the lungs
options.C: Intrapleural pressure increases to force air out of the lungs
options.D: The chest wall pushes inward to compress the lung tissue

question: What is the oily substance produced by sebaceous glands called?

options.A: Keratin

options.D: Sebum

question: What temperature range is known as the 'danger zone' where bacteria multiply quickly in food?

options.D: Seventy to one hundred degrees Celsius

question: What is a major physiological function of the hypodermis?

options.A: Insulating the body against heat loss

options.C: Producing new epidermal skin cells
options.D: Secreting sweat to cool the skin surface

question: What is a major clinical benefit of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) for teenagers?

options.C: They eliminate all risks of contracting viral STIs

question: During a passive range of motion check of the knee, the patient complains of sharp pain. What should you do?

options.C: Stop moving the joint immediately to prevent further injury
options.D: Switch immediately to active range of motion testing

question: Why is the perineal body such an important structure in the pelvic floor?

options.C: It directly controls the hormonal changes that trigger uterine contractions.

question: How should you apply antiseptic skin prep solution to a patient's surgical site?

question: How does home care primarily reduce patient anxiety compared to hospital stays?

options.A: By keeping patients in a familiar environment near loved ones and daily routines
options.B: By guaranteeing that doctors visit the home every single hour
options.C: By stopping family members from visiting during stressful treatment times

explanation: Familiar surroundings and personal routines help lower stress and confusion for recovering patients. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: What distinct shape do the ulcers formed by this parasite in the colon usually take?

options.A: Circular crater ulcers

question: Which drug is given as the specific antidote for a severe paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.D: Atropine

question: What is a key nursing priority when caring for a patient newly diagnosed with a uterine issue causing recurrent miscarriages?

question: What is your duty as a nurse regarding a patient's feelings and mindset during a referral?

options.C: Forcing the patient to leave the clinic immediately without explanation

question: A lab report shows a patient's sputum sample has acid-fast bacilli. Which disease are doctors likely checking for?

question: Which baby position is required for a planned home delivery to be considered safe?

question: What genotype represents a person who carries the sickle cell trait without having the full disease?

question: Which of these steps gives the ultimate, definitive proof that a patient has cervical cancer?

question: A client with an inherited degenerative disorder shows early muscle weakness and clumsy coordination. What should you do first?

question: Which of these is a major duty of a registered dietitian in a hospital?

question: Why must an effective screening program have accessible treatment available?

options.D: Finding a disease is useless if patients cannot get care

explanation: Screening only improves health outcomes if positive results lead to timely, effective medical interventions. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h3)

question: What kind of skin do you usually see in someone with untreated hypothyroidism?

options.A: Flushing and oily patches
options.B: Warm, moist, and smooth skin
options.C: Bronze hyperpigmentation
options.D: Dry, coarse, and cold skin

explanation: A slow metabolism means the sweat and oil glands aren't working at full speed, leaving the skin feeling dry, rough, and chilly.

question: Which imaging test is most commonly used to confirm a diagnosis of osteoarthritis?

options.A: PET scan
options.B: X-ray
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: MRI scan

explanation: X-rays are the standard and most cost-effective way to view joint space narrowing and bone spurs characteristic of osteoarthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h4)

question: How would you describe a patient who is in a state of stupor?

options.A: The patient sleeps constantly unless spoken to softly
options.B: The patient cannot be awakened by any stimulus at all
options.C: The patient is fully awake but confused about the current date
options.D: The patient responds only to vigorous and painful stimuli

explanation: Spot on! A stupor means the person is deeply asleep and will only wake up if you give them strong or painful stimuli.

question: What is a major nursing priority right after a patient has heart valve surgery for endocarditis?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic medications once the patient leaves the operating room
options.B: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise to strengthen the heart muscle
options.C: Restricting fluid intake completely to prevent any swelling
options.D: Monitoring closely for signs of infection and evaluating neurological status for emboli

explanation: Great nursing care here means staying alert! We watch for any lingering infection and check the patient's brain function (neurological status) to catch any loose clots early.

question: What does a pulse oximeter measure non-invasively in a client?

options.A: The rate of cellular metabolism in lung tissue
options.B: The exact amount of carbon dioxide in the blood
options.C: Arterial oxygen saturation levels
options.D: Total hemoglobin concentration in red blood cells

explanation: Pulse oximetry uses light wavelengths to estimate the percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin in peripheral blood vessels. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T2#GNS213_U2_T2_h5)

question: Where is medication placed when using the sublingual route?

options.A: On top of the tongue
options.B: Swallowed with water
options.C: Under the tongue
options.D: Between the cheek and gum

explanation: Sublingual medications are placed specifically beneath the tongue for rapid dissolution and absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h1)

question: Which feature is most essential for a successful adolescent reproductive health clinic?

options.A: Charging high fees to discourage casual visits by teenagers
options.B: Youth-friendly services with strict privacy and non-judgmental staff
options.C: Mandatory reporting of all adolescent clinic visitors to their parents
options.D: Locating the clinic inside high school classrooms during lessons

explanation: Adolescents avoid health facilities if they fear moral judgment or lack of confidentiality from staff. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h6)

question: How do antibodies cause too much hormone to be released in conditions like Graves' disease?

options.A: By mimicking normal regulatory hormones and over-activating receptors
options.B: By blocking hormone breakdown enzymes in the bloodstream
options.C: By shrinking the target gland until it releases stored hormones
options.D: By destroying the pituitary gland to stop feedback loops

explanation: Think of these rogue antibodies as imposters that pretend to be the body's natural signaling messengers, tricking the gland into working overtime. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is the main use of the Nigerian National Formulary?

options.A: To grade medical students on their pharmacology exam scores
options.B: To record the personal contact details of all licensed doctors
options.C: To provide a list of approved and safe medicines for healthcare use
options.D: To set the retail prices for all retail pharmacies in the country

explanation: Think of the formulary as your official handbook! It lists safe, approved medications you can trust when caring for patients in Nigerian hospitals.

question: What is the very first thing you should do the moment an AED arrives?

options.A: Turn on the AED power
options.B: Check the patient for a carotid pulse
options.C: Deliver a manual shock immediately
options.D: Apply the adhesive pads to the chest

explanation: Just flip the power switch! The machine will start talking to you and guide you through every single step, making it super easy to follow.

question: Why do midwives and doctors check a baby's fontanelles and sutures during labour?

options.A: To estimate the exact gestational age of the pregnancy
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the foetus before delivery
options.C: To figure out the position and attitude of the baby's head
options.D: To check if the baby's brain is developing normally in utero

explanation: By feeling these soft spots and lines, you can map out which way the baby's head is facing and how well it is flexing to come down.

question: Roughly what percentage of waste coming out of a healthcare facility is actually considered hazardous?

options.A: 75 to 90 percent
options.B: 10 to 25 percent
options.C: 50 to 60 percent
options.D: 95 to 99 percent

explanation: Most hospital waste is regular everyday trash (like office paper and food wrappers). Only about 10 to 25 percent is truly hazardous and needs special handling. You've got this!

question: Why is teaching a patient to keep a menstrual calendar a helpful nursing action?

options.A: It replaces the need for any further laboratory blood testing
options.B: It serves as a permanent medical cure for abnormal hormones
options.C: It completely prevents the future development of ovarian cysts
options.D: It empowers the patient to track cycle patterns and share accurate data with clinicians

explanation: Data is power! A calendar helps both the nurse and the patient see patterns clearly, spot changes early, and check if treatments are working.

question: What is a major danger of leaving a needle stuck inside a multi-dose medication vial?

options.A: It automatically dilutes the concentration of the liquid drug
options.B: It allows environmental pathogens to enter and contaminate the medicine
options.C: It increases the expiration date of the remaining medicine
options.D: It causes the rubber stopper to dissolve completely into the solution

explanation: Leaving a needle sitting in a vial creates an open doorway for bacteria and viruses to sneak in and multiply. Always remove the needle after drawing up your dose!

question: Right after birth, during which psychological phase does a new mother focus heavily on herself and rely on others for decisions?

options.A: Taking-in phase
options.B: Letting-go phase
options.C: Taking-hold phase
options.D: Depressive phase

explanation: Great thinking! In the 'taking-in' phase right after delivery, the mum is resting, processing her birth story, and letting nurses and family take care of her needs.

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the ICU?

options.A: To replace the function of the human heart
options.B: To assist or take over the work of breathing
options.C: To increase blood pressure in shock patients
options.D: To cure underlying lung diseases permanently

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs! It helps or completely takes over breathing to keep oxygen flowing while the patient's body heals. You've got this!

question: What is a windshield survey during a community assessment?

options.A: An inventory of all drugs available inside the local primary health center
options.B: A laboratory test used to check the purity of drinking water sources
options.C: An observational method where the nurse travels through the community to note environmental conditions
options.D: A written examination given to school children to test their health knowledge

explanation: A windshield survey is a quick observation method where nurses drive or walk through a community to observe housing, sanitation, and resources. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of occupational health surveillance?

options.A: To punish workers who report feeling sick on the job
options.B: To catch early signs of work-related illness through regular testing
options.C: To calculate the exact salary of every factory worker
options.D: To replace the need for engineering safety barriers

explanation: Surveillance monitors worker health over time so that illnesses can be detected and treated early before causing permanent damage. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h7)

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.A: To increase their overall body fat percentage
options.B: To prevent the onset of juvenile diabetes
options.C: To support rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.D: To replace iron lost during monthly menstruation

explanation: Teens growing up face new changes; adolescent girls need extra iron to make up for what is lost during monthly periods and keep anaemia away.

question: Who belongs on the multidisciplinary team supporting a patient's psychosocial recovery?

options.A: Hospital accountants and administrative billing staff
options.B: Pharmacists and surgical instrument sterilization technicians
options.C: Psychologists, occupational therapists, and social workers
options.D: Security guards and hospital maintenance engineers

explanation: Spot on! Comprehensive care needs a team that looks after emotional health, daily independence, and social resources together.

question: Which nail change is most commonly linked to long-term low blood oxygen levels?

options.A: Koilonychia
options.B: Yellowing
options.C: Clubbing
options.D: Paronychia

explanation: You got it! Finger clubbing—where the fingertips broaden and the nail bed softens—happens when the body has dealt with low oxygen for a long time.

question: What is a common misconception about advance care planning in healthcare?

options.A: That patients must pay a fee to create an advance directive
options.B: That doctors must approve every sentence written in a living will
options.C: That it is just a one-time signature on a legal form rather than an ongoing conversation
options.D: That nurses are legally forbidden from talking about living wills

explanation: Advance care planning is a continuous process of communication between patients, families, and providers, not just paperwork. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: What is the main feature that separates stable angina from unstable angina?

options.A: Stable angina lasts for days without any relief
options.B: Unstable angina is always completely cured with exercise
options.C: Unstable angina occurs unpredictably even at rest
options.D: Stable angina causes pain that radiates down both legs

explanation: While stable angina follows a predictable pattern during exertion, unstable angina can happen at rest and represents a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which temporary side effect is very common after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis
options.B: High blood pressure requiring medication
options.C: Chills and low-grade fever
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: You got it! Misoprostol frequently causes mild, temporary side effects like chills, nausea, or a slight fever. They pass quickly!

question: What is the main goal of a rectal washout?

options.A: To measure the exact core body temperature
options.B: To administer liquid nutrition directly to the colon
options.C: To permanently cure chronic lower back pain
options.D: To completely cleanse the lower bowel using fluid cycles

explanation: Think of a rectal washout as a thorough internal clean. It uses repeated cycles of fluid to wash out stubborn stool and debris from the lower colon. You've got this!

question: A newborn baby fails to cry or breathe right after delivery. What do we call this emergency?

options.A: Birth asphyxia
options.B: Neonatal jaundice
options.C: Congenital anomaly
options.D: Infant malnutrition

explanation: When a baby can't breathe on their own at birth, it's called birth asphyxia. Quick resuscitation is the key here—you'll practice this a lot in your midwifery postings!

question: Why would a doctor prescribe corticosteroids for a patient suffering from severe serum sickness?

options.A: To replace missing complement proteins in the bloodstream
options.B: To quickly reduce widespread inflammation and immune activity
options.C: To kill any underlying bacterial infection in the skin
options.D: To permanently destroy the patient's antibody-producing cells

explanation: Corticosteroids act like a calming balm for the overactive immune system, easing the pain and swelling.

question: Which side effect often happens when drugs like metoclopramide and promethazine block dopamine in the brain?

options.A: Severe persistent diarrhea
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Extrapyramidal symptoms
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: You got it! Blocking dopamine can mess with movement control, leading to extrapyramidal symptoms like muscle spasms or restlessness. Always watch your patients for this!

question: During which weeks of pregnancy is the embryo most sensitive to harmful substances (teratogens) that cause birth defects?

options.A: During gametogenesis before fertilization
options.B: The first week prior to implantation
options.C: The final trimester before birth
options.D: Weeks three through eight during organogenesis

explanation: Correct! Weeks 3 to 8 are when all the major organs are actively forming, making this a critical window where they are most vulnerable.

question: What is the most important thing a nurse must make clear during pre-vasectomy counseling?

options.A: Sperm analysis is optional after the first month
options.B: The procedure is intended to be permanent
options.C: General anesthesia will be used in the operating room
options.D: Sexual performance will improve after surgery

explanation: Great job! Patients need to know that a vasectomy is meant to be permanent because reversing it is difficult and costly.

question: What happens when fertilization does NOT take place during the cycle?

options.A: Progesterone drops and the uterine lining sheds
options.B: Progesterone rises and the uterine lining thickens further
options.C: Estrogen disappears completely and ovulation happens again
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin spikes in the blood

explanation: When pregnancy doesn't happen, the corpus luteum fades, progesterone levels fall, and the body sheds the uterine lining as a menstrual period. Totally normal physiology!

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three areas checked in the Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Eye opening response
options.B: Sensory touch response
options.C: Motor response
options.D: Verbal response

explanation: Remember the three main parts of GCS: Eyes, Verbal, and Motor! Sensory touch isn't part of it. A handy trick for exams and the ward.

question: What part do community elders usually play in keeping traditional food beliefs alive?

options.A: They strictly enforce hospital dietary guidelines for patients
options.B: They pass down dietary rules and cultural heritage to younger generations
options.C: They import foreign ingredients to change local diets
options.D: They test new foods in scientific laboratories before cooking

explanation: Elders act as the keepers of tradition, sharing the stories and dietary practices that bind the community together. As nurses, we respect this heritage while promoting health!

question: A patient wants a sleep aid that doesn't cause addiction or slow down the central nervous system too much. Which option is best?

options.A: Traditional benzodiazepines
options.B: Intravenous general anesthetics
options.C: Short-acting barbiturates
options.D: Melatonin receptor agonists

explanation: Melatonin agonists mimic your body's own natural sleep hormone, which helps you avoid the heavy brain-slowdown and addiction risks of stronger pills.

question: How does the contrast dye help visualize the urinary structures during an IVP?

options.A: By speeding up the heart rate to increase blood flow to kidneys
options.B: By dissolving blockages inside the renal pelvis immediately
options.C: By staining the outer skin to track the dye path visually
options.D: By making the structures show up clearly on x-ray images

explanation: Radiopaque contrast dye blocks x-ray beams, creating a clear picture of the urinary tract's interior on the final images. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the most common cause of rectovaginal fistula in developing countries?

options.A: Bladder stones
options.B: Hormonal imbalances
options.C: Chronic appendicitis
options.D: Prolonged and obstructed labor

explanation: Prolonged pressure from the baby's head against the pelvis causes tissue ischemia and necrosis, leading to fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: A patient with viral meningitis asks if they need strong antibiotics. What should you tell them?

options.A: Antibiotics are not prescribed because viral infections do not respond to antibacterial drugs.
options.B: Antibiotics will cure the virus if taken within the first twenty-four hours.
options.C: You need high doses of penicillin immediately to prevent hearing loss.
options.D: Only herbal medications can help clear up viral infections in the brain.

explanation: Remember: antibiotics only kill bacteria, not viruses! For viral meningitis, we focus on supportive care to keep the patient comfortable while their body fights it off.

question: How can a terrible past experience at a hospital affect a patient's future health choices?

options.A: It eliminates all anxiety related to surgical procedures
options.B: It guarantees the person will follow all doctor's orders
options.C: It automatically cures their current physical condition
options.D: It may make the person avoid or delay seeking medical care

explanation: Bad experiences build fear and distrust. As future nurses, we always want to make our clinics welcoming so patients don't run away from care!
